countries.authority: DAAF Guadeloupe (Direction de l'Alimentation, de l'Agriculture et de la Forêt), Saint-Martin/Saint-Barthélemy territorial unit
vaccinations: Rabies (EU rules): primary vaccination at 12 weeks or older, then at least 21 days' wait before entry; boosters must not lapse.
documents: EU non-commercial animal health certificate (5 pets or fewer, owner or authorized person travelling within 5 days), endorsed by APHIS (original ink) and used within 10 days of endorsement for entry. New US certificate versions apply from 1 Oct 2026.

countries.name: Madagascar
countries.summary: Per UK official export guidance, a Madagascar import permit is needed only for unaccompanied pets. Animals need rabies vaccination 30 days–12 months before export, roundworm/tapeworm treatment within 3 days of export, and an official health certificate issued within 48 hours of export. That guidance dates from 1996, and non-official sources also mention a DSV entry authorization and rabies serology, so confirm with Madagascar's veterinary services.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treatment effective against roundworm and tapeworm within 3 days of export; animal free of external parasites at exam (UK official certificate 3951).
countries.import_permit: Per UK official guidance, required only if pets are unaccompanied. Apply to the Director of Animal Production and Sea Fisheries, Antananarivo (title per 1996 guidance; current body likely the Direction des Services Vétérinaires). Non-official sources say all pets need prior entry authorization from the DSV to avoid quarantine.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination ≥30 days before export → request DSV authorization (recommended even if accompanied) → deworming within 3 days and official health certificate within 48 h of departure.
countries.authority: Madagascar veterinary services (Direction des Services Vétérinaires, Antananarivo)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export; vaccination certificate (completed by the vaccinating vet) attached to health certificate (UK official guidance)
documents: Official export health certificate (UK model: OV exam ≤48 h before export; certificate valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Import permit (unaccompanied pets only, per UK guidance)
Exporter declaration that the animal was not imported into the exporting country in the previous 6 months (UK model)

countries.name: Marshall Islands
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.parasite_treatment: USAKA (Kwajalein) only: external parasite treatment (animal and cage) within 5 days before entry.
countries.authority: RMI Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce (national). The USDA page covers only the US Army Garrison Kwajalein Atoll (USAKA).
vaccinations: USAKA (Kwajalein) only: current rabies vaccination on the health certificate.
documents: USAKA (Kwajalein) only: entry request letter, health certificate (e.g. APHIS 7001), proof of spay/neuter; pets enter via Hawaii and must meet Hawaii quarantine rules; register with base Veterinary Services on arrival.

countries.name: North Macedonia
countries.summary: EU-style health certificate for dogs and cats. A titer test is needed only if the pet does not come directly from, or transits, a country outside Annex II. For US origin, APHIS must endorse the certificate within 10 days of travel.
countries.microchip: Required (EU-model certificate: ISO microchip or pre-3 July 2011 tattoo)
countries.rabies_titer: Not required when travelling directly from, or only via, Annex II-listed countries. Otherwise required per the model certificate (≥0.5 IU/ml, ≥30 days after vaccination, ≥3 months before travel)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month (4+ months if titer needed): microchip → rabies (21 days) → certificate within 10 days of travel
countries.authority: Food and Veterinary Agency of North Macedonia (AHV)
vaccinations: Rabies: must be current (EU-model timing: ≥12 weeks old, ≥21 days after primary vaccination)
documents: North Macedonia health certificate for dogs and cats (APHIS-endorsed within 10 days of travel for US origin)
Owner declarations where applicable (unvaccinated young pet; transit through non-Annex II country)

countries.name: Mali
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): rabies vaccination, a vet exam, and a bilingual USDA-endorsed health certificate valid 30 days after issuance. No official rules found for other origins.
countries.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip number recorded if present; not stated as mandatory.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination current → accredited-vet exam and certificate → APHIS endorsement (ink) → travel within 30 days of issuance.
countries.authority: Mali national veterinary services (US-origin certificate per USDA APHIS)
vaccinations: Rabies: required; certificate records date, vaccine, batch and validity end date (no specific timing stated on APHIS certificate)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Mali (English/French), signed by USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement and embossing required); valid 30 days after issuance

countries.name: Myanmar
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Livestock Breeding and Veterinary Department (Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Irrigation)

countries.name: Mongolia
countries.summary: For US origin: a microchip, a current rabies vaccination, and a veterinary health certificate issued by an accredited vet and APHIS-endorsed (valid 30 days after issuance). Rules for other origins were not verified.
countries.microchip: Required (microchip number verified on certificate)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: microchip → rabies vaccination (current) → certificate within 30 days of arrival
countries.authority: General Authority for Veterinary Services of Mongolia / General Agency for Specialized Inspection
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (vaccine name, batch and validity recorded)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Mongolia (US: accredited vet + APHIS endorsement; valid 30 days after issuance)

countries.name: Macao
countries.summary: An IAM import licence is required. Dogs and cats must be at least 4 months old, microchipped, rabies-vaccinated and have a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml (sample ≥3 months before export). Since 12 June 2026, pets from rabies-affected countries that meet the pre-entry requirements and pass IAM inspection on arrival no longer do the former 30-day quarantine.
countries.microchip: Required. Implanted before the rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: At least 0.5 IU/ml at an IAM-approved lab. Sample taken at least 30 days after the latest rabies vaccine and at least 3 months before export (US-origin rules per APHIS; rabies-free origins may differ, so confirm with IAM).
countries.import_permit: Yes. Import licence from the Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM) before travel.
countries.quarantine: From 12 June 2026: none for compliant pets from rabies-affected countries that pass IAM vet inspection on arrival (previously a mandatory 30 days). Non-compliant pets: expect quarantine or refusal.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccine → titer sample ≥30 days later → wait ≥3 months → IAM licence → health certificate within 10 days of travel → government endorsement.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Tibetan Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa and their crosses. Bengal cats need 5th generation or later domestic ancestry stated on the certificate. Domestic dogs and cats only.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. Arrange the IAM vet inspection at Macau International Airport in advance. Note: Macao is in Hong Kong's Group IIIA, so onward travel to Hong Kong means at least 30 days of HK quarantine.
countries.export: IAM issues export health certificates. Contact IAM in advance and meet the destination's requirements.
countries.authority: Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM / Instituto para os Assuntos Municipais)
vaccinations: Rabies: 30 days to 1 year before export (per APHIS summary of IAM requirements).
documents: IAM import licence. The importer named on the health certificate must match the licence holder.
Official health certificate for Macao (one per animal), valid 10 days from issue, government-endorsed
Rabies vaccination record and titer lab report

countries.name: Northern Mariana Islands
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.export: For export to New Zealand, MPI treats the Northern Mariana Islands as Category 3 (same as the US mainland), per USDA.
countries.authority: CNMI Department of Lands and Natural Resources (Division of Agriculture / quarantine)

countries.name: Martinique
countries.summary: A French overseas department in the EU. APHIS states the entry requirements are the same as for France (EU rules): ISO microchip, rabies vaccination at least 21 days before entry, and an EU animal health certificate endorsed by APHIS. A titer test is needed only from non-EU-listed countries.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip implanted and scanned before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: Only from non-EU-listed third countries: blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before travel, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Not needed from the US or Canada.
countries.import_permit: Not under EU non-commercial rules. Confirm any DAAF prior-declaration requirement.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5 weeks before travel from the US. From non-listed countries, add 3+ months for the titer.
countries.restricted_breeds: French dangerous-dog law: category 1 attack-type dogs cannot be imported. Confirm with DAAF.
countries.authority: DAAF Martinique / French Ministry of Agriculture
vaccinations: Rabies: primary at 12 weeks or older, then at least 21 days before entry; boosters must not lapse.
documents: EU non-commercial health certificate (up to 5 pets), APHIS-endorsed with an original ink signature, used within 10 days of endorsement. New US versions apply from 1 Oct 2026.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: obtain written requirements from Mauritania's veterinary services or embassy before booking.
countries.authority: Mauritania veterinary services (ministry responsible for livestock) – not verified

countries.name: Montserrat
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: obtain written conditions from the Department of Agriculture, Brades (tel. 664-491-2075).
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Lands, Housing & the Environment – Department of Agriculture (Veterinary Services)
documents: No APHIS country page and no published import conditions on gov.ms. The Department of Agriculture offers veterinary and sanitary/phytosanitary services. Montserrat is rabies-free (listed as 'no rabies-risk' by the Cayman Islands), so permit and titer requirements are likely, but they're unconfirmed.

countries.name: Malta
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry. Dogs also need tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before entry. Pre-notification of every pet arrival to the Veterinary Regulation Directorate is mandatory.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis with praziquantel (or proven equivalent) given by a vet 24-120 hours before scheduled entry and recorded in the passport/certificate. Not required for dogs moving directly from FI, IE, NO, Northern Ireland. Cats: none.
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> tapeworm treatment for dogs 24-120 h before arrival -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified in official sources.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Air point of entry: Malta International Airport (Luqa) (list dated 2010). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Veterinary Regulation Directorate (VRD)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Mandatory 'Pets Arrival Notification' (pre-notification of arrival) to the VRD for commercial and non-commercial movements; entry is denied if not done. Required notice period not confirmed from the official page (secondary sources cite 24 h to 3 working days) - submit well ahead.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Mauritius
countries.summary: Import permit from the Veterinary Services (Ministry of Agro-Industry) is required before shipment. Requirements include a rabies titer at least 3 months before travel, a sterilisation certificate, manifest-cargo arrival with a local broker, and a minimum 5-day quarantine at Réduit. Several dog breeds are banned.
countries.microchip: Required (verified on the certificate). ISO 11784/11785 recommended.
countries.rabies_titer: Required for dogs and cats: FAVN or RFFIT ≥0.5 IU/ml at a lab approved by the exporting country, or a WOAH reference lab. Blood sample at least 4 weeks after vaccination. Travel no earlier than 3 months after sampling, and the test must be no more than 12 months before shipment. The lab must also send results directly to the Mauritius veterinary services. Alternative: 6 months in an approved quarantine station in the exporting country.
countries.parasite_treatment: External parasite treatment, within coverage at export (US certificate).
countries.import_permit: Mandatory: 'No animal should be embarked for Mauritius without an import permit.' Apply to petimport@govmu.org at least 3 months before departure. Issue depends on quarantine kennel availability. Fees: Rs 500 import fee plus Rs 500 veterinary clearance per animal.
countries.quarantine: Minimum 5 days at the government Quarantine Facility, Réduit, at the owner's cost (kennel Rs 15/day; the owner supplies food and litter). An older permit template mentioned up to 1 month depending on origin.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4-5 months: microchip → rabies vaccination → titer test 4+ weeks later → wait 3 months from sampling → apply for the permit 3+ months ahead → dog Ehrlichia/Brucella tests within 45 days → health certificate and endorsement → email flight details 4+ days before arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (Animal Welfare Act 2013, 4th Schedule): American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Terrier, Blue Nose Pit Bull, Red Nose Pit Bull, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Boerboel. Other 'dangerous' breeds (e.g. Rottweiler, Doberman, Cane Corso, Bull Mastiff, Rhodesian Ridgeback, Alaskan Malamute, Kangal) are allowed only if pure-bred.
countries.private_aviation: High impact. Official guidelines: all pets must arrive as manifest CARGO ONLY (not in cabin, not as excess luggage), with a local customs broker present at the airport. Without a broker, the animal may be sent back at the owner's cost. A private flight must manifest the pet as cargo and arrange the broker and veterinary pickup at SSR International.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agro-Industry, Food Security, Blue Economy and Fisheries – Division of Veterinary Services / Livestock and Veterinary Division (petimport@govmu.org)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine per manufacturer. US-origin certificate: at least 3 months of age, more than 2 months before export for a primary vaccination, or at least 30 days for a booster.
Dogs: distemper, infectious hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus – up to date, given more than 14 days before dispatch
Cats: feline enteritis (panleukopenia), rhinotracheitis, calicivirus – between 14 days and 12 months before export
documents: Import permit (number and date shown on the veterinary certificate)
International veterinary certificate from the exporting country's competent authority (US: APHIS-endorsed)
Rabies vaccination certificate and RNATT lab report (endorsed by the competent authority)
Dogs: Ehrlichia canis (IFAT, negative at 1:40) within 45 days before departure, and a negative Brucella canis test
Sterilisation certificate (except breeding animals with a pedigree and breeder's licence)
Application form per animal, motivation letter to the Principal Veterinary Officer, owner's passport copy, copy of the vaccination book

countries.name: Maldives
countries.summary: DOGS ARE PROHIBITED (no exceptions). Cats need an import permit from the Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture, rabies and core vaccinations, parasite treatment and an official health certificate.
countries.parasite_treatment: Cats: internal and external parasite treatment between 1 month and 14 days before expected arrival (UK DEFRA export guidance).
countries.import_permit: Yes for cats (per UK DEFRA export guidance for Maldives). Dogs: import prohibited.
countries.timeline: Cats: plan at least 6 weeks: vaccinations (rabies ≥30 days before) → import permit → parasite treatment 14–30 days before arrival → clinical exam and health certificate shortly before export.
countries.restricted_breeds: All dogs prohibited ('import of dogs and dangerous animals is strictly prohibited', Velana airport customs guide).
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. The dog ban applies to all arrivals, including private jets and resort transfers. Cats are cleared by the quarantine officer at the arrival port (Velana International Airport).
countries.authority: Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture (live animal imports); Maldives Customs Service
vaccinations: Cats: rabies 30 days to 12 months before export
Cats: feline calicivirus, feline viral rhinotracheitis, feline panleukopenia
documents: Import permit (application with pet passport or vaccination card showing rabies, FCV, FVR and FPL vaccinations)
Official export health certificate. The UK version requires a clinical exam within 72 hours of export.
On arrival: commercial invoice approved by Maldives Customs, plus airway bill or bill of lading, given to the port quarantine officer

countries.name: Malawi
countries.summary: Malawi's Animal (Import) Rules require a written import permit from the Chief Veterinary Officer for any animal. UK official guidance adds rabies vaccination 30 days–12 months before export and an official health certificate issued within 14 days of export. That guidance dates from 1996, so confirm current details with the CVO.
countries.import_permit: Required for all animals under the Animal (Import) Rules (Control and Diseases of Animals Act). Written permit from the Chief Veterinary Officer, P O Box 30372, Lilongwe; the CVO may attach conditions.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: apply to CVO for permit → rabies vaccination ≥30 days before export → official health certificate within 14 days of export → notify CVO of arrival date/flight.
countries.private_aviation: UK guidance: for air travel, report the arrival date and flight number to the Chief Veterinary Officer, Lilongwe, before departure. For a private flight, give the aircraft registration/flight details and arrival airport.
countries.authority: Chief Veterinary Officer, Department of Animal Health and Livestock Development (Malawi)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export; certificate must show animal description, vaccine batch number and production laboratory (UK official guidance). Cats must be vaccinated before export; dogs from rabies-free Great Britain may instead be vaccinated on arrival.
documents: Import permit from Chief Veterinary Officer, Malawi
Official export health certificate (exam ≤14 days before export, UK model)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration of no contact with a rabid animal in the 6 months before export

countries.name: Mexico
countries.summary: From the US: cats need no health certificate (since 16 Dec 2019), but since 3 Aug 2026 dogs need an 'NWS Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs' signed by a USDA-accredited vet no more than 5 days before entry (no APHIS endorsement). SENASICA (OISA) inspects all dogs and cats on arrival for disease signs, ectoparasites and wounds.
countries.parasite_treatment: The pet must be free of ectoparasites at the SENASICA inspection. If ticks are found, they are sampled and removed, and the pet is held at OISA until cleared, at the importer's cost. Other ectoparasites must be treated by a vet of the owner's choice.
countries.import_permit: Not required for personal pets. A 'Pet Program – Frequent Traveler' registration is available.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel: book a USDA-accredited vet for the NWS inspection within 5 days of the flight; arrange the Mexican-side screwworm certificate for the return to the US.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation specifics are published. SENASICA/OISA inspects at the point of entry, so confirm with the FBO and handler that SENASICA inspection is available at the arrival airport and time.
countries.export: Returning or entering the US from Mexico: dogs need a screwworm-freedom certificate. For Mexico, a SENASICA-authorized clinical vet (MVRA directory) may sign it, with inspection within 5 days. Mexico is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, so the CDC Dog Import Form route applies.
countries.authority: SENASICA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad, Inocuidad y Calidad Agroalimentaria), OISA inspection offices
vaccinations: No rabies certificate is listed as an entry requirement on the APHIS Mexico page (Sep 2026). Carry rabies proof anyway for the US return.
documents: Dogs: NWS (New World screwworm) Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs, issued no more than 5 days before entry by a USDA-accredited vet. No APHIS endorsement. Don't list cats on the dog form, or the form becomes invalid.
Cats: none.
Carriers must be clean; bedding, toys and food beyond the arrival day are removed.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.summary: A MAQIS import permit is needed. Pets from 'scheduled' countries (list updated by DVS on 11 Dec 2025) can enter without quarantine. Pets from all other countries need a rabies vaccination before export and at least 7 days of quarantine on arrival, which DVS can extend up to 6 months. Sabah and Sarawak have their own state veterinary authorities and rules.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip required under the DVS regulations for non-scheduled countries.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required in the DVS regulations for Peninsular Malaysia (antibody levels may be tested at random during quarantine). Sabah and Sarawak may differ; not verified.
countries.import_permit: Yes: MAQIS import permit. Restricted dog breeds also need prior written approval from the MAQIS Director General.
countries.quarantine: Non-scheduled countries: at least 7 days in quarantine, which can be extended up to 6 months case by case. Scheduled countries: no quarantine per the DVS pet portal. Scheduled list (DVS notice of 11 Dec 2025): United Kingdom, Eire, Northern Ireland, New Zealand, Japan, Sweden, Brunei, Singapore, Greece, Luxembourg, Czech Republic, Malta, Slovenia, Estonia, Bahrain, Austria, Belgium, Germany, Portugal, Montenegro, Bulgaria, Lithuania. Australia appeared in the older list but is not in the Dec 2025 list; confirm with DVS.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies vaccine (30+ days before entry), MAQIS permit, government-endorsed health certificate within 7 days of export, then quarantine on arrival unless from a scheduled country.
countries.restricted_breeds: Banned dogs: Akita, American Bulldog, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Neapolitan Mastiff, Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier). Restricted dogs (need MAQIS approval, pedigree, premises inspection, personal pet or security use only): Bull Mastiff, Bull Terrier, Doberman, German/Belgian/East European Shepherd, Perro de Presa Canario, Rottweiler. Minimum age 3 months.
countries.private_aviation: The DVS regulation says pets must be carried by aircraft or other transport directly to the prescribed landing place or any other airport in Malaysia. No rule specific to private aircraft was found. Confirm the arrival airport and the quarantine officer's attendance with MAQIS/DVS.
countries.authority: Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services (MAQIS). Sabah and Sarawak: state veterinary departments (Sarawak: dvs@sarawak.gov.my)
vaccinations: Rabies (non-scheduled countries): approved vaccine before export. The DVS pet portal says at least 30 days before entry.
Other core vaccines given within 12 months before export, as recommended by a licensed vet.
documents: MAQIS import permit (ePermit)
Pet passport or certificate with full description and identification

Veterinary health certificate from the exporting country's government veterinary authority: examination within 7 days before export, no rabies in the country for the previous 6 months, not imported into the country within the previous 6 months
Rabies vaccination certificate
Scheduled countries: Malaysian veterinary certificate and airline captain's affidavit (per DVS portal)

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.summary: Pets need rabies vaccination within 12 months before export and an official health certificate (US: valid 30 days; UK: exam within 48 h of export). Since April 2024, Mozambique bans the import of listed dangerous dog breeds and their crosses unless authorized by the National Director of Livestock Development.
countries.parasite_treatment: For US-origin pets (APHIS): animal must be free of external parasites at exam; routine treatments up to date.
countries.import_permit: General pet import permit not stated in APHIS/UK guidance. Dangerous-breed dogs need prior authorization from the National Director of Livestock Development (MADER).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel (longer for listed breeds): rabies vaccination ≥30 days before export → check breed list/apply for authorization → official health certificate (US: ≤30 days; UK: exam ≤48 h).
countries.restricted_breeds: April 2024 MADER measure (reported by state news agency AIM) bans import of potentially dangerous breeds and crosses, including Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Pit Bull, Rottweiler, American Staffordshire Terrier, Tosa Inu, Saint Bernard, Bull Terrier, Akita Inu, Doberman, Kangal, Bullmastiff, and others. Exceptions need authorization, e.g. assistance dogs, security dogs, and sterilized companion dogs over 2 years. Dogs must be at least 3 months old and registered within 10 days of entry. Sterilization is required.
countries.authority: National Directorate of Livestock Development (DNDP), Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MADER)
vaccinations: Rabies: within 12 months before export (US/APHIS); UK guidance: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export. US certificate allows pups/kittens under 3 months travelling with the mother's rabies certificate.
Routine vaccinations/treatments up to date (APHIS certificate)
documents: Official export health certificate: For US-origin pets (APHIS): USDA-endorsed certificate (April 2024 form) valid 30 days after issuance, attesting no rabies on premises of origin for 12 months; UK: OV exam within 48 h of export
Rabies vaccination certificate
Authorization from National Director of Livestock Development for dangerous breeds (where allowed)

countries.name: Namibia
countries.summary: Pets from countries other than South Africa and Botswana need a veterinary import permit from the Directorate of Veterinary Services, Windhoek. The permit is valid 4 months and single use. After the exporting vet endorses it, the owner must obtain a 'landing permit' before travel. Pets from South Africa need only an inter-territorial movement permit and rabies vaccination.
countries.microchip: Not mandated by the DVS portal (microchip if transiting a country requiring it). The US dog certificate uses tag/tattoo/description.
countries.parasite_treatment: US-origin dogs: heartworm treatment (ivermectin, milbemycin, moxidectin, selamectin or DEC) from the negative test until export, and continued for 6 months after arrival. The owner must bring 6 months of supply because it is not easily available in Namibia.
countries.import_permit: Required except for South Africa-origin pets (residence of 3+ months). Apply via Vet.Permits@mawlr.gov.na. Fee N$150 (or €50 at a Namibian mission). Processed within a maximum of 3 working days. Valid 4 months, single use.
countries.quarantine: None for EU/USA, South Africa and SADC origins. 30-day quarantine on arrival for pets from other countries (per the Namibia Trade Portal).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks: rabies vaccination (30+ days ahead) → apply for the permit (≤3 days) → courier the permit to the exporting vet → dog blood tests within 30 days of export → health certificate and endorsement within 10 days → email documents to obtain the landing permit before departure.
countries.private_aviation: The permit names the state veterinary office responsible for inspection. Arrange inspection at the arrival airport (normally Hosea Kutako International) in advance. No official manifest-cargo rule found.
countries.export: To South Africa: inter-territorial movement permit from a local state vet. To Botswana: health certificate from a state vet. To the EU: state vet health certificate, microchip and rabies titer. Others: destination permit required.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform – Directorate of Veterinary Services (Vet.Permits@mawlr.gov.na)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before travel. Under 3 months old: the dam's vaccination is accepted and the pet must be vaccinated at 3 months in Namibia.
Full vaccination status expected (EU/USA origin)
documents: Namibian veterinary import permit (number on the health certificate)
Health certificate from the exporting country's state vet (US: USDA-endorsed, exam within 10 days of export)
Rabies vaccination record
Dogs (US/EU and other origins): negative tests within 30 days of export for Brucella canis, Babesia gibsoni, Dirofilaria immitis, Leishmania (and T. evansi for non-US origins)
Landing permit from the Namibian state vet (send the endorsed permit, pet passport and lab results before travel)
From South Africa: inter-territorial movement permit from the local state vet. From Botswana: Veterinary Certificate of Identity, Rabies Vaccination and Movement Permit.

countries.name: New Caledonia
countries.summary: Direct import is allowed only from France, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland, Belgium, French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna, Fiji, Vanuatu, Australia and New Zealand, with an import permit and a country-specific health certificate. Arrivals then spend 10 days in public quarantine at Païta. Pets from any other country must first spend 6 months in France, or go through quarantine in Australia or New Zealand.
countries.rabies_titer: Required per the certificate where applicable, and only at a DAVAR-listed approved laboratory (results from other labs are refused). Timing not stated on the page.
countries.import_permit: Yes, for every dog or cat import (SIVAP/DAVAR).
countries.quarantine: 10 days in public quarantine (CPZP, Païta) on arrival for domestic carnivores from France or Pacific countries. For other origins the length is set by species and origin; confirm with SIVAP (+687 41 25 36, davar.sivap-qsa@gouv.nc).
countries.timeline: Plan at least several months (6+ months for non-listed countries routed via France): permit, certificate, approved-lab titre where required, book quarantine.
countries.restricted_breeds: No breed ban was listed on the DAVAR page. A brachycephalic breed list carries flight-welfare conditions.
countries.authority: DAVAR – Service d'inspection vétérinaire, alimentaire et phytosanitaire (SIVAP)
vaccinations: Per the country-specific health certificate.
documents: Import permit (form I.DPA.NC.15/12)
Country-specific dog or cat health certificate
Rabies antibody result from an approved lab where required
Brachycephalic breeds: vet fitness-to-fly certificate and larger crate

countries.name: Niger
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: obtain written requirements from Niger's veterinary services or embassy before booking.
countries.authority: Direction Générale des Services Vétérinaires (Ministry of Livestock, Niger) – pet rules not verified

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.summary: Pets need an import permit from the Federal Department of Veterinary and Pest Control Services (FMARD, Abuja). Required documents: an officially endorsed health certificate, rabies vaccination within 1 year (inactivated vaccine), and a rabies serology result. NAQS verifies the permit and inspects the animal on arrival.
countries.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): all pets must be microchipped. UK certificate accepts a microchip or permanent tattoo.
countries.rabies_titer: FMARD lists a laboratory rabies serology result as a permit document. UK certificate requires ≥0.5 IU/ml, with the sample taken 3–24 months before export. The APHIS US certificate does not include a titer statement. Plan for a titer regardless of origin.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Director, Dept of Veterinary and Pest Control Services, FMARD Abuja (hard copy or vpcs@fmard.gov.ng) using the application form with travel date. Fee: N5,000 per dog/cat via Remita. Processing ~3 working days; permit valid 14 days from issue. These details come from the FMARD page as indexed by search; fmard.gov.ng was unreachable (HTTP 525) on 2026-10-13.
countries.quarantine: NAQS inspects imported dogs/cats at the port of entry and verifies the permit and veterinary certificate. Under the NAQS SOP, live animals may be held for quarantine observation (NAQS or owner's facility); animals suspected of disease may be held 2–3 weeks; non-compliant or illegal animals may be seized or destroyed.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 months before travel if a titer is needed (UK model: sample ≥3 months before export). Steps: microchip → rabies vaccination → titer → apply for FMARD permit (~3 days, valid 14 days) → endorsed health certificate → notify NAQS of permit and arrival date.
countries.private_aviation: NAQS SOP: notify NAQS of the import permit details and arrival date, and declare the animal for NAQS inspection at the point of entry. Arrange NAQS presence at the arrival airport/FBO in advance.
countries.authority: Federal Department of Veterinary and Pest Control Services (FMARD) and Nigeria Agricultural Quarantine Service (NAQS)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine, record not more than 1 year old (FMARD); For US-origin pets (APHIS): within one year of departure with a US-approved inactivated vaccine; UK certificate: given at ≥3 months of age, ≤1 year before export
documents: Import permit (DVPCS/FMARD)
Health certificate signed by attending vet and endorsed by official vet of exporting country (US: APHIS ink endorsement, valid 30 days; UK: exam ≤48 h, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination record
Rabies serology lab result
Proof of permit fee payment

countries.name: Nicaragua
countries.summary: Pets need a USDA-endorsed health certificate (exam within 2 weeks; original plus 1 copy) with rabies vaccination no more than 365 days before embarkation for animals over 4 months, and parasite treatment. No import permit for personal pets, but a quarantine permit is obtained at the port on arrival.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treated for endo- and ectoparasites with approved products (no timing stated).
countries.import_permit: Not required for personal pets (commercial shipments need one). A quarantine permit is obtained at the port of entry on arrival.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: rabies within 365 days, vet exam within 2 weeks, USDA ink endorsement (allow mail time).
countries.export: Return to the US: Nicaragua is NOT on the CDC high-risk list (Apr 2026). It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Instituto de Protección y Sanidad Agropecuaria (IPSA)
vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 4 months, no more than 365 days before embarkation. The rabies certificate accompanies the health documents.
documents: Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, exam within 2 weeks of departure, endorsed by APHIS (original ink signature and embossing). Present the original plus 1 photocopy on arrival. No notary or consular stamp.
Rabies certificate.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national breed ban identified. Cropping/docking is banned in NL; a 2026 draft would bar cropped/docked dogs born on/after 1 Dec 2016 from shows - status and any effect on visiting dogs not confirmed; check with NVWA if the dog is cropped/docked.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry (NVWA list v1.0.4, 16 Dec 2024): Amsterdam Schiphol, Eindhoven, Rotterdam, Maastricht-Aachen, Groningen Eelde, Lelystad. Passengers with animals must use the red 'something to declare' exit. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Norway
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry. Dogs also need tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before entry. Norway applies EU pet rules via the EEA; customs red channel is mandatory.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: Echinococcus treatment (praziquantel) by a vet 24-120 h before arrival, recorded in passport, even for day trips (e.g. from Sweden). Exempt: dogs arriving directly from Finland, Ireland, Malta (and Northern Ireland per EU rules). Frequent travellers may use a regular treatment schedule at intervals of max 28 days (at least two treatments before entry). Cats: none.
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> tapeworm treatment for dogs 24-120 h before arrival -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (incl. any cross): Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Czechoslovakian Wolfdog. Customs says import requires a special police permit applied for in advance; police may order euthanasia or removal of non-compliant dogs.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Pets from outside the EU/EEA may only arrive via Oslo Airport Gardermoen (or Storskog road crossing, Kirkenes). Always use the customs red channel (by air, even from Sweden). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: Leaving Norway for EU/EEA: EU pet passport (EEA rules). To third countries: destination rules; contact Mattilsynet.
countries.authority: Norwegian Food Safety Authority (Mattilsynet); Norwegian Customs
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: Norway does NOT accept unvaccinated young pets from EU states; never from third countries.

countries.name: Nepal
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: Unverified. Sources conflict on whether a Department of Livestock Services permit is needed (possibly only for 3 or more pets).
countries.quarantine: Unverified. Reportedly none if compliant.
countries.private_aviation: Unverified: entry reportedly via Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu) with the animal quarantine office notified in advance.
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Services / Animal Quarantine Office (Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development)
vaccinations: Unverified (secondary sources): rabies at least 30 days before arrival
documents: Unverified: health certificate within about 10 days of travel, government-endorsed

countries.name: Nauru
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Nauru Government (agriculture/quarantine services)

countries.name: Niue
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (DAFF), Niue – Quarantine

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.summary: Pets from Australia (Category 1) need no quarantine. Pets from Category 2 (rabies-free) and Category 3 (rabies absent or well controlled) countries need an MPI import permit, a pre-booked quarantine place, and at least 10 days of quarantine. They must arrive by air as manifested cargo at Auckland or Christchurch only. Non-categorised countries are not eligible directly. A new Import Health Standard (2026) applies alongside the 2021 one until 31 March 2027 and is mandatory from 1 April 2027.
countries.microchip: Microchip required. 2026 IHS official identity check: Category 2, microchip scanned by an official vet at least 6 months before shipment. Category 3, official scan before the RNATT sample (twice, the first at least 6 months before shipment, if the RNATT is taken 3-6 months before shipment). Mandatory for all arrivals from 1 April 2027; the ID check process started on 1 October 2026.
countries.rabies_titer: Category 3 (2026 IHS): RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/mL on a sample taken 3-12 months before shipment.
countries.parasite_treatment: 2026 IHS: internal parasites treated twice (first within 30 days of shipment and at least 14 days before the second; second within 5 days of shipment). Ticks and fleas: last treatment within 16 days of shipment with continuous protection. Dogs also need heartworm prevention and tests for Babesia gibsoni, Brucella canis (entire dogs), Leishmania, leptospirosis and others, per the IHS.
countries.import_permit: Required for Category 2 and 3 (including assistance dogs). Book quarantine first and attach the booking form. Allow 30 working days after all documents are received (USDA says at least 20 business days).
countries.quarantine: At least 10 days at an MPI-approved transitional facility for Category 2/3, longer if extra tests or treatments are needed or the period ends outside business hours. Book before the permit application. Australia and assistance dogs are exempt.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 7-8 months for Category 3 (6-month ID check, RNATT 3+ months before shipment, quarantine booking, then permit 30 working days) and 6-7 months for Category 2 (6-month ID check). Australia: weeks.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Brazilian Fila, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, American Pit Bull Terrier type. Hybrid dogs and cats (other than Bengal) need EPA approval. Approximate minimum ages: 8 weeks (Category 1), 12 weeks (Category 2), 9 months (Category 3). Not more than 42 days pregnant.
countries.private_aviation: The 2026 IHS says a cat or dog arriving by air must travel as manifested cargo (only assistance dogs excepted) and may arrive only at Auckland or Christchurch. Category 2 crates must carry a government seal. MPI has no specific private-aircraft guidance. A pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the IHS, so arrange manifested-cargo status with MPI before booking.
countries.export: NZ-origin pets need the MPI veterinary (export) certificate or Animal Welfare Export Certificate (AWEC), which is also required to re-enter as an 'NZ-origin' pet. Short trips of 30 days or less use a simplified short-stay certificate.
countries.authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), Biosecurity New Zealand
vaccinations: Rabies (Category 3): at 12 weeks of age or older, continuously valid; a primary vaccination must be at least 6 months before shipment (2026 IHS).
Category 2: no rabies vaccination required.
documents: MPI import permit
Signed quarantine booking form
Category 3: rabies vaccination records, RNATT result, Category 3 Rabies Certification Form
Pre-export ID check notified by the exporting competent authority directly to MPI
Government-endorsed veterinary certificate; vet exam within 2 days of shipment

countries.name: Oman
countries.summary: A prior veterinary import permit is required, applied for through the Customs Bayan system (MAFWR Veterinary Quarantine). Pets must be over 4 months old with a full vaccination record, microchip, and rabies antibody test (RNATT/FAVN) from an accredited lab.
countries.microchip: Electronic microchip number must be shown on the immunisation record.
countries.rabies_titer: Required: RNATT or FAVN from an accredited lab. Sample drawn 21–30 days after the last rabies vaccination. The result must be at least 3 months and no more than 12 months old at export.
countries.import_permit: Required before arrival via Customs Bayan, issued by MAFWR Veterinary Quarantine Department. Fee OMR 20. Approval within about 2 hours during official hours, 7 days a week. Validity is not stated.
countries.quarantine: Not stated. Shipment release takes about 2 hours after inspection (24/7).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet 12 weeks or older) → titre blood draw 21–30 days later → wait until the titre result is at least 3 months old → Bayan import permit → government health certificate → arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited under Resolution 222/2019 (including mixes): Pitbull, Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Rottweiler, Doberman Pinscher, Presa Canario, Boxer, Boerboel, Caucasian Shepherd Dog, Anatolian Karabash, Great Dane. Pets must be over 4 months old.
countries.private_aviation: The official customs page lists arrival documents for land, sea, air cargo or passenger ports, which suggests that accompanied (passenger) arrivals are accepted. In-cabin carriage on private jets is not specifically addressed, so confirm with Muscat airport veterinary quarantine.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth and Water Resources (MAFWR) – Veterinary Quarantine Department, via Royal Oman Police Customs (Bayan)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccinated after 12 weeks of age. No more than 12 months may have passed since vaccination at the time of import.
Full immunisation record since birth (with a photo of the pet) must be submitted.
documents: Veterinary import permit (Bayan)
Government veterinary health certificate from the exporting country
Passport or immunisation record
Accredited lab certificate for the rabies antibody test

countries.name: Panama
countries.summary: Pets need an APHIS-endorsed health certificate that is then stamped and signed by a Panamanian consulate or embassy. Rabies vaccination from 3 months of age, with at least 30 days after the first dose. Pets under 4 months are not admitted. Send a Home Quarantine Request to MINSA at least 3 days before arrival.
countries.quarantine: Home quarantine under a MINSA request.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies (30-day wait if first dose), health certificate, APHIS endorsement, consular stamp, MINSA request at least 3 days before arrival.
countries.export: Return to the US: Panama is NOT on the CDC high-risk list. It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Control de Zoonosis / Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario (MIDA)
vaccinations: Rabies: from 3 months of age; at least 30 days must pass after the first rabies vaccination before entry.
documents: International health certificate for dogs or cats (forms dated June 2025), signed by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by APHIS.
Panamanian consulate/embassy stamp and signature after APHIS endorsement (apostille requirement temporarily waived since 31 Dec 2020, but the consular stamp is still required).
Home Quarantine Request (MINSA form) with a scanned health certificate, arrival date/time and flight, emailed to cam@minsa.gob.pa at least 3 days before arrival.

countries.name: Peru
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an original official sanitary export certificate from the origin country stating current vaccinations and internal/external deworming within 30 days; SENASA inspects on arrival (fee S/ 98.60) at Jorge Chávez, other international airports or land border posts.
countries.microchip: Not required by SENASA Peru for entry (not listed).
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 30 days before travel, stated on the origin certificate.
countries.import_permit: No separate import permit for pet dogs and cats; SENASA performs documentary check and clinical inspection on arrival.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: vaccinations → deworming within 30 days → official origin certificate → SENASA inspection and payment on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: SENASA offices at Jorge Chávez (Lima Hub office open 24/7 incl. holidays) and other international airports; confirm SENASA attendance for private arrivals at regional airports.
countries.export: Leaving Peru: SENASA issues the sanitary export certificate per destination requirements; submit ≥72 h before travel: request, destination requirements/permit, vet health certificate and vaccination certificate (Colegio Médico Veterinario format), payment S/ 97.20, any destination tests/microchip; clinical inspection. Offices: Lima Hub (Callao, 24/7), Ate, Lurín and regional offices. Contact viajacontumascota@senasa.gob.pe.
countries.authority: SENASA Perú (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agraria) – MIDAGRI
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory for dogs and cats from 3 months of age.
Dogs: canine parvovirus, distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis (plus rabies).
Cats: feline panleukopenia (plus rabies).
documents: Application with owner and pet data
Original sanitary export certificate (international sanitary certificate) from the origin country's official authority stating vaccinations, deworming and health status
Payment for entry inspection (S/ 98.60)

countries.name: French Polynesia
countries.summary: An import permit from the Direction de la Biosécurité (online, about 7 months before departure) is required. Pets from non-rabies-free countries also need a rabies titre with a 3-month wait, dogs need a leishmaniasis test, and pets get two parasite treatments. Dogs and cats must travel as manifested cargo, with inspection at Tahiti only. Category 1 dogs are banned.
countries.microchip: Identification certificate showing the implantation date is required.
countries.rabies_titer: For non-rabies-free origins: blood taken at least 1 month after vaccination, at an accredited lab. The result is valid from 3 months after sampling, for 1 year. Pets vaccinated at 3 months cannot enter before 9 months and 21 days of age.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments by a vet: first within 30 days of departure (no later than 16-19 days before), second at least 14 days later and within 4 days of departure.
countries.import_permit: Yes, online at mes-demarches.gov.pf (separate procedures for air and sea arrivals). Apply about 7 months before departure. Without a direct flight, each leg needs its own application.
countries.quarantine: No quarantine period is stated. The pet gets an inspection and laissez-passer by the DBS official vet at Tahiti (fees about 6,000-12,500 XPF depending on arrival time).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 7 months: microchip, rabies vaccine, titre (1+ month after the vaccine, then a 3-month wait), permit application, leishmaniasis test and parasite treatments in the last 30 days, health certificate within 4 days of departure.
countries.restricted_breeds: Category 1 dogs (attack dogs under French classification) are prohibited. Pets under 3 months are not admitted unless with their mother. Snub-nosed breeds may be refused by airlines.
countries.private_aviation: DBS states that dogs and cats must travel to French Polynesia as manifested cargo in sealed IATA crates; only certified assistance dogs may travel in the cabin. Inspection is done only at Tahiti. Private aircraft are not specifically addressed; a pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the stated rule. Confirm with DBS (zoo.aeroport.dbs@administration.gov.pf).
countries.export: DBS publishes a separate page for exporting a pet from French Polynesia (not reviewed in detail).
countries.authority: Direction de la Biosécurité (DBS), Cellule zoosanitaire
vaccinations: Rabies: a primary vaccination is valid from 21 days after injection. Boosters must be given before the previous one expires, with the same vaccine.
documents: Import permit (mes-demarches.gov.pf; 5,500 XPF per animal)
Identification certificate
Rabies vaccination certificates
Rabies titre result
Dogs: negative leishmaniasis ELISA/IF within 30 days of departure, sent directly to DBS (the permit is issued only after this)
Females: non-pregnancy ultrasound within 30 days of departure, or a sterilisation certificate
Official export health certificate signed within 4 days of departure

countries.name: Papua New Guinea
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: National Agriculture Quarantine and Inspection Authority (NAQIA)

countries.name: Philippines
countries.summary: Every dog and cat needs an SPSIC import clearance from the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), applied for online through the DA Trade System (11 working days), and current rabies vaccination. Personal imports are limited to 3 animals per importer per year. From 1 January 2027 a rabies antibody titre test becomes mandatory for all applications.
countries.microchip: Microchip required (number recorded on the SPSIC and used to track repeat imports). Pets arriving without the required identification are refused entry and returned (consular sources).
countries.rabies_titer: Not currently required. Mandatory for all SPSIC applications from 1 January 2027 (BAI). Test details (lab, timing, wait) were not yet published on the pages reviewed.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment records are uploaded with the application. They need not be renewed before applying, but must remain valid until arrival.
countries.import_permit: Yes: SPSIC from BAI via the DA Trade System. Processing takes 11 working days and the permit is valid 60 days (BAI FAQ). A permit issued after the pet's departure date is invalid. A new permit is needed if the airline changes in transit.
countries.quarantine: BAI's pet import page sets no quarantine. The pet is inspected at the port of entry.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks (more for 2027 arrivals because of the titre test): microchip, rabies vaccine (14-day wait if first dose), SPSIC application (11 working days), health certificate, travel within SPSIC validity.
countries.restricted_breeds: Minimum age 4 months. No pregnant animals. Animals that have given birth must have done so at least 12 weeks before travel. No breed bans found on BAI pages.
countries.authority: Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), National Veterinary Quarantine Services Division
vaccinations: Rabies: given by a licensed vet in the source country at 12 weeks of age or older. After a first-ever vaccination, wait 14 days before applying. Annual boosters: can ship at once if given within the vaccine's validity, otherwise wait 14 days. 3-year vaccines are accepted.
Rabies may be waived for pets from WOAH self-declared rabies-free countries.
BAI says only rabies vaccination is required.
documents: SPSIC (BAI import clearance)
Vaccination and antiparasitic records
Microchip number and an actual photo of the pet
Pet passport if any
Veterinary health certificate from the origin country matching the SPSIC (animal count must match)
One-time importers: notarised Affidavit of Undertaking (BAI MC 43, 2020)

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.microchip: Unverified (secondary sources): ISO 11784/11785 microchip.
countries.rabies_titer: Unverified (secondary sources): not required.
countries.parasite_treatment: Unverified (secondary sources): internal and external parasite treatment within 14 days before entry.
countries.import_permit: Unverified. Secondary sources say an NOC/permit is needed. Pakistan's Animal Quarantine Department was reportedly merged into the National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority (NAFSA) in 2025.
countries.quarantine: Unverified. Reportedly none if documents are in order.
countries.authority: Ministry of National Food Security & Research (Animal Quarantine Department / NAFSA)
vaccinations: Unverified (secondary sources): rabies 30 days to 12 months before arrival
documents: Health certificate from a licensed vet (APHIS: USDA endorsement not required for US-origin pets)
Unverified: import permit / NOC

countries.name: Poland
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types. Poland has a national list of aggressive breeds requiring a permit for residents (not reviewed).
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry (2016 ordinance): Warsaw Chopin (Okęcie), Warsaw Modlin, Kraków, Katowice, Gdańsk, Poznań, Wrocław, Łódź, Rzeszów, Szczecin-Goleniów, Bydgoszcz, Lublin (Świdnik); customs performs checks. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: General Veterinary Inspectorate (GIW)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Puerto Rico
countries.summary: A US territory. From the US mainland (interstate): no permit, but an official CVI from an accredited vet (valid 30 days), rabies vaccination for pets over 4 months, external-parasite treatment within 72 hours, and ID are required. International arrivals must also meet CDC/USDA federal rules.
countries.microchip: Official individual ID required: microchip OR collar with metal tag.
countries.parasite_treatment: External parasite treatment within 72 hours before entry, recorded on the health certificate.
countries.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats moving interstate.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1–2 weeks before travel: rabies status check, CVI within 30 days, parasite treatment within 72 hours of arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries CANNOT enter the US via Puerto Rico (no CDC-registered facility in US territories).
countries.export: Puerto Rico to the US mainland is domestic travel (no CDC form). The Cayman Islands classes Puerto Rico as high rabies risk (3-month titer wait).
countries.authority: Departamento de Agricultura de Puerto Rico – Oficina del Oficial Estatal de Sanidad Animal (SAHO)
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs and cats over 4 months must be vaccinated and carry a rabies certificate. The Puerto Rico Department of Agriculture document says the vaccination must be given 'within six (6) months prior to shipment', which is unusually strict, so confirm with the PR State Veterinarian.
documents: Official certificate of veterinary inspection (e.g. APHIS 7001 or a state CVI) by an accredited vet, valid 30 days from inspection, stating the animal doesn't come from a rabies-quarantined area.
Rabies vaccination certificate.
International arrivals: CDC Dog Import Form and other federal requirements (see the US entry).

countries.name: Palestine
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.private_aviation: No operating airport in Palestinian territory. Access is via Israeli-controlled entry points (e.g. Ben Gurion, see IL) or Jordan (Allenby/King Hussein Bridge), so the transit country's rules apply.
countries.authority: Unknown (Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture)

countries.name: Portugal

No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.

countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified in official sources (Portugal has a potentially-dangerous-dog licensing regime for residents).
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry (DGAV list): Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Beja, Cascais, Funchal (Madeira), Ponta Delgada, Terceira and Santa Maria (Azores). Contact emails per airport are on the DGAV list (e.g. Lisbon pcflisboaa@dgav.pt, Faro pets.entrypoint.fao@dgav.pt). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
