To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Directorate-General for Food and Veterinary (DGAV)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Arrivals from non-EU countries: Portugal requires owners to contact the authorities at least 48 hours before arrival using the written arrival notice form (per USDA APHIS).
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Palau
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Bureau of Agriculture, Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and the Environment (biosecurity)

countries.name: Paraguay
countries.summary: Paraguay applies Mercosur GMC Res. 20/24: an original CVI from the origin country's official veterinary authority (valid 60 days) presented to a SENACSA inspector on arrival. Up to 5 animals per person count as pets.
countries.microchip: Not mandatory under Mercosur rules; if electronic ID is used it must be ISO 11784/11785 with location stated on the CVI.
countries.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum internal and external antiparasitic treatment within 15 days before CVI issue (Mercosur GMC 20/24).
countries.import_permit: Not required for up to 5 dogs/cats; 6 or more are treated as a commercial live-animal import.
countries.quarantine: None routinely; non-compliance may lead to refusal, re-export or retention (owner's cost). Paraguay may refuse animals diagnosed with leishmaniasis.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: rabies (≥21 days if primary) → antiparasitic within 15 days of CVI → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI → SENACSA check on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Present the pet and CVI to the SENACSA veterinary inspector at the point of entry; confirm inspector attendance for private arrivals.
countries.export: Leaving Paraguay: SENACSA issues the CVI via SENACSA Digital (account validated in person once with notarised ID) or in person; private-vet clinical inspection within 10 days before CVI using SENACSA's 'Certificado de Inspección Clínica y Vacunación' form; rabies valid ≤1 year, ≥21 days if primary. EU/UK/Israel/Russia/UAE CVIs processed in person.
countries.authority: SENACSA (Servicio Nacional de Calidad y Salud Animal)
vaccinations: Rabies: animals 90 days or older, valid vaccine; primary vaccination at least 21 days before embarkation.
Under 90 days: allowed if CVI certifies age and no contact with urban rabies in the last 90 days.
documents: Original CVI (Mercosur model) from origin official authority, valid 60 days from issue while rabies is valid
Clinical exam within 10 days before CVI issue
Or official passport endorsed by origin authority with all CVI data

countries.name: Qatar
countries.summary: An import permit from the Ministry of Municipality (Animal Resources / Livestock Department) is required before arrival. Rabies vaccination and a rabies titre lab report must be submitted with the application. NZ MPI notes a one-pet-per-person policy and a list of prohibited dog breeds.
countries.microchip: Required in practice. NZ MPI guidance requires the microchip to be scanned and verified before the rabies vaccination. ISO 15-digit is recommended.
countries.rabies_titer: Required: the import permit application must include a laboratory report for a rabies titre test (NZ MPI, Aug 2024). Third-party sources cite at least 0.5 IU/ml and a 90-day wait after the blood draw, which is not confirmed officially. Whether titre rules vary by origin is unclear.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Ministry of Municipality (Livestock Department / Department of Animal Resources) as a hybrid online or offline service. Processing about 1 working day. Valid 30 days from issue. NZ MPI says the permit should be issued at least 30 days before arrival. One pet per person (NZ MPI, Aug 2024). Third-party sources say permits go only to residents or those holding work visas. Unverified: a visitor (Hayya) permit route reported in 2022 required pets over 7 months old. Hukoomi states pets must be over 4 months old.
countries.quarantine: No mandatory quarantine if health requirements are met. Otherwise quarantine at the owner's expense (NZ MPI).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccination → titre blood test → apply for MoM import permit (issued at least 30 days before arrival, valid 30 days) → official health certificate → arrive via Hamad International Airport.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs (NZ MPI Aug 2024 list): Afghan Hound, American Staffordshire Terrier, Boerboel, Boxer, Bull Terrier, Bulldog, Chinese Shar-Pei, Doberman, Great Dane, Japanese Akita, Neapolitan Mastiff, Rottweiler, Staffordshire Bull Terrier. Large or dangerous breeds may also need Ministry of Interior permission (2022 report, unverified).
countries.private_aviation: NZ MPI states dogs and cats may enter only via Hamad International Airport (DOH). In-cabin travel is accepted with written airline permission. Private jets commonly use Doha International (DIA). No official confirmation was found that pets can clear at DIA, so verify with MoM and the handler before routing a private flight there.
countries.authority: Ministry of Municipality – Livestock Department / Department of Animal Resources
vaccinations: Rabies: required. Valid 30 days after a primary vaccination (NZ MPI). Hukoomi says vaccinations must be at least 30 days before travel. Upper limit generally within 12 months (third-party).
Other core vaccines (distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis and leptospirosis for dogs; FVRCP for cats) are reported by third parties but not confirmed in an official Qatari text.
documents: Ministry of Municipality import permit (valid 30 days from issue, per Hukoomi)
Original official veterinary health certificate from the exporting country
Rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies titre lab report
Copy of owner ID

countries.name: Réunion
countries.summary: Réunion is a French overseas department and part of the EU, so EU pet rules apply. From mainland France or the EU: microchip, valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. From non-EU countries: EU animal health certificate. A rabies titer is needed for every African origin except Mauritius and Saint Helena.
countries.microchip: Required (implanted before or at the rabies vaccination). A legible tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is accepted.
countries.rabies_titer: Required for pets from non-listed third countries (all of mainland Africa, Madagascar, Comoros, Seychelles, etc.): ≥0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated lab. Sample at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 90 days (3 months) before the health certificate is issued. Not required from the EU, or from listed territories such as Mauritius and Saint Helena.
countries.quarantine: None if EU rules are met. Non-compliant animals may be refused, returned or isolated at the owner's cost.
countries.timeline: From non-listed countries plan at least 4 months: microchip → rabies vaccination → titer 30+ days later → wait 3 months → EU health certificate within 10 days of arrival. From the EU: microchip + vaccination 21+ days before travel.
countries.restricted_breeds: French law: category 1 'attack' dogs (pit-bull, Boerbull and Tosa types without a pedigree) may not be imported into France. Category 2 dogs are subject to conditions.
countries.private_aviation: Pets from outside the EU must pass a documentary and identity check at a designated travellers' point of entry. Confirm with DAAF Réunion that the arrival airport (Roland Garros/Pierrefonds) and the private/FBO terminal can do the check. Max 5 animals for non-commercial movement.
countries.export: Leaving for other countries follows the destination's rules. The EU pet passport is issued by a Réunion vet.
countries.authority: DAAF de La Réunion (Direction de l'alimentation, de l'agriculture et de la forêt) – French Ministry of Agriculture
vaccinations: Rabies: at 12 weeks of age or older, after microchipping. Valid from 21 days after the primary vaccination. Boosters must be given within validity.
documents: From the EU: EU pet passport

From non-EU countries: EU animal health certificate (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, Annex III; old 577/2013 certificates are valid if issued before 1 Oct 2026), endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority, valid 10 days until the entry check
Owner's written non-commercial declaration
Titer lab report (non-listed origins)

countries.name: Romania
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified in official sources.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry: Bucharest Henri Coandă (24/7) and Cluj Avram Iancu (on request). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: National Sanitary Veterinary and Food Safety Authority (ANSVSA)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries. (Romania: non-commercial yes, commercial no.)

countries.name: Serbia
countries.summary: EU-model certificate for up to 5 pets: microchip and a valid rabies vaccination (21-day wait after primary). A titer test is needed only from, or via, non-listed countries. For US origin, the certificate must be issued and APHIS-endorsed within 10 days of travel (within 24 hours if more than 5 pets).
countries.microchip: Required (permanent marking by microchip; tattoo accepted only if applied before 3 July 2011)
countries.rabies_titer: Only if coming from, or transiting, a non-listed country: ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before import
countries.parasite_treatment: Echinococcus treatment optional for entry into Serbia (APHIS)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month from listed countries (4+ months otherwise): microchip → rabies (21 days) → certificate within 10 days of travel
countries.private_aviation: APHIS notes Serbia restricts imports/transit from Germany and Hungary over foot-and-mouth disease; avoid routing via DE/HU with animals until confirmed this does not apply to pets
countries.authority: Veterinary Directorate, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of Serbia (Uprava za veterinu)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccine with ≥1 antigenic unit/dose (WHO); for a primary vaccination, 21 days must pass before entry; boosters within validity
Pets under 16 weeks: accepted only with owner declaration of no contact with wild rabies-susceptible animals, or accompanied by vaccinated mother
documents: Serbia certificate for non-commercial movement of ≤5 dogs/cats/ferrets (separate form for >5) — valid for 4 months after issue for onward movement, or until rabies vaccine expiry
Owner's non-commercial declaration
Pet passport from origin country (Serbian government tourism page)

countries.name: Russia
countries.summary: EAEU rules: up to 2 personal dogs/cats with an international pet passport (rabies and core vaccines, clinical-exam mark within 14 days of departure) need no permit or quarantine. Without a passport, or for unaccompanied pets, an EAEU Form 15 certificate is needed. More than 2 pets needs a permit (annual Form 1 permit covers up to 5). Flights are heavily restricted by sanctions.
countries.microchip: Not required by Rosselkhoznadzor for import (unidentified pets may be imported for home keeping); recommended
countries.rabies_titer: Not required (only an alternative to proof of valid vaccination)
countries.parasite_treatment: Not required
countries.import_permit: None for ≤2 personal dogs/cats with owner. >2 animals or unaccompanied: Rosselkhoznadzor permit via Argus system; annual generic Form No. 1 permit covers up to 5 pets from listed countries (non-commercial)
countries.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → clinical exam/stamp within 14 days (passport) or 5 days (Form 15) → enter via a border point with veterinary control
countries.restricted_breeds: No import ban found. Russia has a government list of potentially dangerous dog breeds subject to keeping/walking rules (not verified in this research)
countries.private_aviation: Heavily restricted: reciprocal airspace bans with EU/UK/US/Canada and others; US/EU/UK export controls and sanctions bar many business jets (US-origin or Western-registered/operated) from flying to Russia. Check with Elysium Jet operations before quoting. Entry only at border points with veterinary control. APHIS also notes temporary transit restrictions via Germany/Hungary for FMD-susceptible animals (not dog/cat specific)
countries.export: Rosselkhoznadzor: check destination rules; microchip (ISO) and rabies vaccination as required by destination; titer at approved lab for EU, Switzerland, UAE, Japan, Israel, Turkey, US (dogs) etc. Obtain Form No. 1 veterinary certificate from district state vet station (СББЖ) via Mercury, ≤5 days before departure. At airport veterinary control (or in advance at Rosselkhoznadzor offices/VGNKI, up to 5 days ahead, or online via ecert.vetrf.ru) exchange for EU certificate, Form 5a or destination-specific export certificate. No permit for owner-accompanied pets. Within EAEU (BY/KZ/AM/KG) Form 1 suffices. Rosselkhoznadzor guidance does not mention any cultural-value certificate for pedigree dogs; no current official source found requiring one
countries.authority: Rosselkhoznadzor (Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance), applying EAEU common veterinary requirements
vaccinations: Rabies: all dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before dispatch unless vaccinated within last 12 months; 3-year vaccine accepted if vet confirms still valid; or titer ≥0.5 IU/ml
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis (or dihydrostreptomycin prophylaxis) — ≥20 days before, within last 12 months
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days before, within last 12 months
Unvaccinated puppies/kittens <3 months: only with Form 15 certificate
documents: ≤2 pets accompanied by owner: international veterinary passport with vaccination records and stamp of the origin country's competent authority confirming clinical exam within 14 days before shipment (serves as the veterinary certificate)
Otherwise: EAEU Veterinary Certificate Form 15 (US: APHIS-endorsed, exam within 5 days per APHIS guidance; APHIS page states Russia allows exam up to 14 days before)

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.summary: RAB issues veterinary import permits (official). The pet-specific details come from a non-official source: rabies vaccination 30 days–12 months before entry, a government-endorsed health certificate, internal parasite treatment shortly before entry, and arrival via Kigali International Airport. Confirm with RAB.
countries.microchip: Non-official sources conflict (ISO 11784/11785 required vs. only recommended).
countries.rabies_titer: Not required for entry, per non-official sources.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal parasite treatment within 1–5 days before entry (non-official source).
countries.import_permit: RAB lists 'Veterinary import/export/transit permits' among its services (official). A non-official source says applications go through the RAB e-portal with a RWF 15,000 fee. Contact info@rab.gov.rw, +250 788 385 312, toll free 4675.
countries.quarantine: Non-official: none if compliant; non-compliant pets may be quarantined, returned or euthanized at owner's expense.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: apply for RAB permit → rabies vaccination ≥30 days before entry → deworm 1–5 days before entry → endorsed health certificate within ~10 days of arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Non-official: give veterinary officials at Kigali International Airport prior notice of arrival so an inspector is available.
countries.export: Pets leaving Rwanda need an international veterinary certificate signed by an official veterinarian of RAB (Rwanda migration authority travel page).
countries.authority: Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before entry (non-official source)
documents: Veterinary import permit (RAB)
Health certificate issued/endorsed by government vet of origin country, within ~10–14 days of arrival (non-official, sources conflict)
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.summary: A MEWA pet entry/exit permit is required, applied for through the Naama platform (naama.sa) before shipment and valid 30 days. Cats and dogs must be at least 4 months old, microchipped, and carry an original government health certificate and a rabies vaccination with at least 6 months of validity remaining.
countries.microchip: Electronic microchip or other means of identification (MEWA Naama guide). The 2021 MEWA rules require a passport and an electronic microchip, and the microchip number must appear on the vaccination record uploaded with the application.
countries.rabies_titer: Not mentioned in MEWA's official documents (2021 rules, Naama guide). Some third-party guides claim a titre is needed, but this is unverified. Confirm on Naama for the specific origin country.
countries.parasite_treatment: Pets must be free of external parasites and diseases (2021 MEWA rules). No specific treatment window is stated.
countries.import_permit: Required: 'Pet entry and exit permit (dogs, cats)' on naama.sa (login via Nafath). Apply 15 days before shipment (MEWA user guide). IATA Traveldoc says at least 5 days before departure, so allow 15. Valid 30 days from issue. Entry only through the port named on the permit. Individuals: one permit every 6 months, maximum 2 animals per permit. Applicant age: at least 21 for dogs and at least 18 for cats (the older 2021 rules said at least 30 for dogs). Diplomats are exempt from the age rule with an official letter. Commercial dog imports are not allowed. Import only from countries listed as permitted on the platform. MEWA may set arrival times according to quarantine capacity.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated for compliant pets. MEWA may schedule arrival according to port quarantine capacity. The GCC veterinary quarantine law applies.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip → rabies vaccination (must have at least 6 months of validity left at entry) → Naama permit application at least 15 days before shipment (valid 30 days) → government health certificate and certificate of origin → enter only via the named port.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including crosses): Pit Bull, Rottweiler, Boxer, Mastiff, Tosa, Bulldog, Perro de Presa Canario. Minimum pet age: 4 months. Historical note: USDA's page still says dogs are 'not generally allowed' except for hunting, guarding or guiding the disabled. That is outdated compared with MEWA's current Naama service, which allows individuals aged 21 or over to import pet dogs of permitted breeds.
countries.private_aviation: Not addressed in official sources. MEWA requires entry through the port named on the permit and IATA-compliant containers for air imports. Make sure the permit names the actual private-aviation arrival airport (e.g. the Riyadh or Jeddah executive terminals) and confirm MEWA veterinary inspection availability with the handler.
countries.export: The same Naama 'pet entry and exit permit (dogs, cats)' service covers departures, with the same conditions (30-day validity, apply about 15 days ahead). The destination country's rules also apply.
countries.authority: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), Naama platform
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination, with at least 6 months of validity remaining (MEWA Naama service conditions). MEWA checks validity when issuing the permit.

Other vaccines according to the exporting country's approved vaccination programme (2021 MEWA rules). Third-party guides cite DHPPi or similar for dogs and FVRCP or similar for cats (not verified officially).
documents: MEWA/Naama pet entry permit (copy or original)
Original government veterinary health certificate from the exporting country, or a digitally endorsed copy for US origin
Original or electronic certificate of origin (no Saudi embassy attestation needed, per the 2021 rules)
Vaccination record or pet passport
For the application: owner's ID, passport or iqama, pet photo, and passport or vaccination page showing the microchip number

countries.name: Solomon Islands
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Biosecurity Solomon Islands (Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock)

countries.name: Seychelles
countries.summary: Veterinary import permit is required for every dog and cat. All pets are quarantined on arrival: a minimum of 2 weeks if conditions are met, otherwise 6 months or return. Pets from rabies-affected countries need rabies vaccination plus a titer. Arrival must be as manifest cargo.
countries.microchip: Microchip number required on the application. ISO standard not stated in the official text.
countries.rabies_titer: Required for animals from rabies-affected countries: RNATT >0.5 IU, at least 1 month after the primary vaccination and no more than 6 months before departure. Copy submitted with the permit application.
countries.parasite_treatment: Not specified in the official conditions. Heartworm is endemic in Seychelles; prevention is advised but not required.
countries.import_permit: Mandatory. Apply at least 4 MONTHS ahead (rabies-infected countries) or 4 WEEKS ahead (rabies-free countries). Issued within 7 working days once complete. Valid 1 month from the intended arrival date, for one consignment only. Applications go to the National Biosecurity Agency (2024 form; older conditions name the Seychelles Agricultural Agency).
countries.quarantine: Mandatory for all: minimum 2 weeks at the single Mahé quarantine station (SR 1,000 per 2 weeks, including the permit, collection and kennel). Animals not meeting conditions face 6 months of quarantine or return. Book quarantine at least 2 weeks ahead and confirm 24 h before arrival.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4-5 months from rabies-affected countries: microchip → rabies vaccination → titer 1+ month later → apply 4 months ahead → book quarantine 2+ weeks ahead → health certificate → arrive as manifest cargo → 14 days of quarantine.
countries.restricted_breeds: No breed ban, but listed breeds and their crosses must be surgically sterilised before entry (e.g. Akita, Alsatian/German Shepherd, Pit Bull types, Staffordshire types, Boerboel, Bulldog, Bullmastiff, Cane Corso, Doberman, Dogue de Bordeaux, French Bulldog, Great Dane, Rottweiler, Shar Pei, Tosa, Tibetan Mastiff and others).
countries.private_aviation: Official conditions: all animals must travel as manifest cargo, preferably on a direct or approved scheduled flight, in an IATA-compliant container. A Veterinary Officer collects them at the airport. Private-jet arrivals must manifest the pet as cargo and pre-arrange pickup with Veterinary Services. Confirm acceptance of a private flight in advance.
countries.authority: National Biosecurity Agency (formerly Seychelles Agricultural Agency – Veterinary Services)
vaccinations: Rabies (rabies-affected countries): inactivated vaccine at 3 months of age or older. Booster between 30 days and 12 months before export. Not mandatory for rabies-free origins.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis, leptospirosis
Cats: panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus
All vaccinations at least 2 weeks before departure
documents: Veterinary Import Permit
Official health certificate (English or French) from the exporting veterinary authority
Rabies vaccination certificate and RNATT result (rabies-affected origins)
Official certificate of no rabies in the locality of origin for the past 6 months
Sterilisation certificate for listed breeds
Import permit from the Ministry of Finance for customs clearance

countries.name: Sudan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Unknown (national veterinary authority not confirmed)

countries.name: Sweden
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Only two points of entry (2020 list): Stockholm-Arlanda and Gothenburg-Landvetter airports. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Swedish Board of Agriculture (Jordbruksverket)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.summary: Rules depend on the origin's AVS schedule. Schedule I (AU, NZ, IE, UK): no quarantine. Schedule II (e.g. USA, Canada, Japan, Hong Kong, most of Western Europe, New Caledonia): no quarantine if the pet arrives within 5 days of the owner and has lived with them for 6+ months, otherwise at least 10 days of quarantine. Schedule III (everywhere else): at least 30 days at the Animal Quarantine Centre (AQC). Every pet needs a dog/cat licence and an AVS import licence.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784 or ISO 11785 Annex A. The chip number must appear on all vaccination and treatment records.
countries.rabies_titer: Schedule II and III: rabies serology of at least 0.5 IU/ml. The blood sample must be taken at least 28 days after a valid vaccination, and between 90 days and 12 months before export. The lab must be a WOAH reference lab or one approved by the competent authority of a Schedule I or II country.
countries.parasite_treatment: Parasite treatments and the veterinary health certificate must both be done 2 to 7 days before export, as set out in the schedule-specific veterinary conditions.
countries.import_permit: Yes: an AVS import licence (personal: S$50 normal, 2 working days; S$100 express, 1 working day), valid 90 days. The dog or cat licence must be obtained first. The USDA summary says to apply 30 days before arrival.
countries.quarantine: Schedule I: none. Schedule II: none if the pet arrives less than 5 days after the owner's entry and has lived at the owner's address for 6+ months; otherwise at least 10 days of home quarantine (smart collar, S$29/animal/day, apply via FormSG first) for personal imports, or 10 days at AQC for commercial imports. Schedule III: at least 30 days at AQC (Sembawang), booked through the Quarantine Management System once the serology result is ready.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4-7 months for Schedule II/III (serology must be at least 90 days before export), and about 1 month for Schedule I. Steps: microchip, rabies vaccine, serology (28+ days after vaccine), book AQC if Schedule III, dog/cat licence, import licence, book inspection 5+ days before arrival, vet certificate and treatments 2-7 days before export.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog), Akita, Boerboel, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, and crosses of any of these. Cats: F1-F4 Bengal or Savannah crosses are prohibited. Housing limits apply (e.g. HDB flats). Minimum age 12 weeks at export.
countries.private_aviation: AVS describes air clearance only at the Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine Station (Changi Airfreight Centre). In-cabin or excess-baggage pets must be in a rigid IATA crate (no soft bags). AVS does not mention Seletar or private aircraft. One FBO arrival guide (Universal Aviation, not official) says pets are accepted at Seletar under the same AVS licence and inspection rules. Confirm with AVS and the FBO where the inspection will happen before routing to Seletar.
countries.export: AVS publishes separate 'Exporting dogs and cats' procedures (avs.nparks.gov.sg). Not reviewed in detail here.
countries.authority: Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS), National Parks Board (NParks)
vaccinations: Rabies (Schedule II and III only): valid inactivated or recombinant vaccine, with no lapse in cover. Schedule I pets need no rabies vaccine or serology.
Dogs: canine distemper, adenovirus type 1, parvovirus type 2.
Cats: feline calicivirus, herpesvirus-1, panleukopaenia.
Schedule III pets are vaccinated against rabies again on arrival at AQC.
documents: Dog licence or cat licence (PALS), obtained before the import licence
AVS import licence via GoBusiness (valid 90 days, cannot be extended)
Veterinary health certificate in the schedule-specific format: Sections I-III by the treating vet, Section IV endorsed by an official government vet, issued 2-7 days before export
Vaccination records and rabies serology report
Signed captain's declaration endorsed by the airline (Schedule I/II)
Customs GST In-Payment permit where applicable
Inspection appointment booked at least 5 days before arrival via AVS e-services

countries.name: Saint Helena
countries.summary: Per the most recent official guidance found (April 2013), dogs and cats may be imported directly only from the UK (and Ascension). Pets from elsewhere, including South Africa, must first enter the UK under UK rules, then obtain a St Helena certificate via DEFRA/APHA with additional blood tests. St Helena no longer offers quarantine. Rules may have changed since the airport opened; confirm with SHG Biosecurity.
countries.microchip: Required under the UK-route protocol.
countries.rabies_titer: Required under the UK entry protocol for non-listed countries (blood test 30+ days after vaccination, 3-month wait).
countries.import_permit: Contact the SHG Biosecurity Officer (julie.balchin@sainthelena.gov.sh, tel +290 24724). Import licence forms exist for regulated goods.
countries.quarantine: No quarantine service on St Helena (abolished 2011). Direct imports from countries other than the UK/Ascension are not eligible under the 2013 guidance.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 months from non-UK origins (2013 guidance: 5-6 months from South Africa via the UK).
countries.private_aviation: High impact and unverified. The 2013 guidance predates St Helena Airport (2017). A direct private flight from Africa with a pet may be refused. Get written confirmation from SHG Biosecurity/Veterinary Section before booking.
countries.export: 2013 guidance: pets could not return directly from St Helena to South Africa and had to travel via the UK. Check current South African permit conditions.
countries.authority: St Helena Government – Biosecurity / Veterinary Section, Agriculture & Natural Resources Division (ANRD)
vaccinations: Rabies: per UK entry rules, then St Helena certificate conditions
documents: St Helena export health certificate agreed with UK DEFRA/APHA (issued by a UK Official Veterinarian)
Additional blood test results required by St Helena (about 1 month)

Points of entry listed on gov.si (not reviewed in detail - confirm arrival airport). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary Sector and Plant Protection (UVHVVR)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry (2017 list): Bratislava, Košice, Piešťany, Poprad, Sliač, Žilina. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.

Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: San Marino
countries.summary: San Marino is an EU Annex I listed territory (pets from it enter the EU without titer test or point-of-entry check). No dedicated official import page was found; in practice pets arrive via Italy, so that country's EU entry rules apply (microchip, rabies vaccination, EU pet passport or EU health certificate; titer test from unlisted countries).
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. (as required by the EU country of arrival)
countries.rabies_titer: Per EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
countries.parasite_treatment: None identified (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None identified if EU requirements are met.
countries.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified.
countries.private_aviation: No airport in San Marino. Nearest jet airports are in Italy; Rimini (Miramare) and Bologna are on Italy's September 2026 list of pet points of entry for third-country arrivals.
countries.export: Leaving: EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport/certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement). Local export procedure not verified.
countries.authority: San Marino veterinary service (Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale); not verified
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): get a Senegalese import permit (valid 3 months), make sure rabies vaccination is current, and travel with a health certificate (APHIS 7001) issued within 21 days of travel. No official rules were found for other origins.
countries.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock and valid 3 months from issue. Per APHIS, apply by email to dsvmepa@gmail.com (cc wadesanou@gmail.com) with country of origin, species and breed, owner's name and address of origin.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4-6 weeks before travel: apply for the import permit, then rabies vaccination at least 21 days before travel if it is a primary dose, then a health certificate within 21 days of travel.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock (Direction des Services Vétérinaires)
vaccinations: Rabies: required; a primary vaccination must be given at least 21 days before travel (APHIS, US-origin)
documents: Import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock
Health certificate (APHIS 7001 accepted for US-origin pets) issued within 21 days of travel; no APHIS endorsement needed if a USDA-accredited vet signs it and adds their national accreditation number
Valid rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.summary: Pets need a licensed-vet health certificate (exam within 30 days, no USDA endorsement or consular stamp) and rabies vaccination no more than 365 days before embarkation for animals over 2 months. A MAG import permit (before travel or on arrival) and a quarantine permit at the port are required.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treated for endo- and ectoparasites with approved products (no timing stated).
countries.import_permit: Required, from the Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal (MAG). Can be obtained before travel or on arrival at the port of entry. A quarantine permit is also obtained at the port on arrival.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel: rabies (within 365 days), vet exam within 30 days.
countries.export: Return to the US: El Salvador IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country (USDA-endorsed CDC certification before leaving the US, or arrival at a CDC-registered facility airport). A screwworm certificate is also needed.
countries.authority: Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería (MAG) – Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal
vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 2 months, vaccinated no more than 365 days before embarkation. The certificate states the date and product.
documents: Health certificate by a licensed vet, exam within 30 days of departure, in at least duplicate. No USDA endorsement, notary or consular stamp.
Rabies vaccination certificate.

countries.name: Sint Maarten (Dutch part)
countries.summary: Get an Animal Movement/Import permit from Inspectorate TEATT (Unit LVV), valid for entry within 30 days, plus an endorsed international health certificate. Pets must be 15 weeks or older, microchipped, rabies-vaccinated at least 21 days before departure and parasite-treated. Dogs and cats from South and Central America (except Suriname) are prohibited.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip, or a readable tattoo applied before July 2011. The number must be on the certificate.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal: negative fecal flotation, or if positive, treatment 21 days before departure. External: parasiticide (e.g. Frontline, NexGard, Bravecto) 7–14 days before departure; free of Amblyomma and Boophilus ticks.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to Inspectorate TEATT – Unit LVV (LVV@sintmaartengov.org) via sintmaartengov.org.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: rabies at least 21 days before departure, fecal test and deworming, permit, tick treatment 7–14 days before departure, APHIS endorsement.
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier types are permitted only if neutered or spayed (stated on the certificate).
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation specifics are published. The USDA-hosted version mentions inspection by a licensed vet within 24 hours of arrival, which isn't in the 2022 conditions, so confirm with LVV.
countries.authority: Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport & Telecommunication (TEATT) – Inspectorate, Unit LVV
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days and no more than 1 or 3 years (per the vaccine) before departure.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, Bordetella and parvovirus.
Cats: FeLV, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia and pneumonitis.
documents: Sint Maarten import permit (valid 30 days from issue).
International health certificate in English or Dutch, from an accredited vet and endorsed by the exporting country's Chief Veterinary Officer (APHIS, via VEHCS). EU pet passports are NOT accepted.
Copy of the owner's passport; Animal Movement Authorization Form if the owner isn't travelling.

countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel. Verify the current situation and requirements with operations, as the administrative situation may have changed.
countries.authority: Unknown (Syrian Ministry of Agriculture / Syrian Customs)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination certificate required (timing not specified).
documents: Health certificate in English, authenticated in the origin country
Rabies vaccination certificate

The government site (gov.sz) was unreachable. Most routings transit South Africa, which requires its own veterinary import permit for dogs and cats.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 8–12 weeks before travel: confirm with Eswatini Ministry of Agriculture, Veterinary Services whether an import permit is needed for the pet's origin; check South African transit rules if routing via South Africa.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Veterinary and Livestock Services, Eswatini

countries.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
countries.summary: An import permit from the Department of Agriculture (Animal Health Services) is required, applied for with an APHIS-endorsed international health certificate that is valid 10 days from issue. The US and Canada are treated as NOT rabies-free. Several dog breeds are banned.
countries.import_permit: Required for all pets. Email, fax or post the application to the Department of Agriculture, Animal Health Services Division, Providenciales (agriculture@gov.tc, +1 649 946 5801).
countries.quarantine: No standard quarantine is published. Non-compliant animals may be held, deported within 48 hours at the owner's expense, or euthanized.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: vet certificate and APHIS endorsement, then the permit application within the 10-day certificate validity, then at least 48 hours' notice of arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, American Staffordshire Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, Fila Brasileiro. Restricted (contact TCI first): Appenzeller, Aryan Molossus, Bandog, Beauceron, Belgian Mastiff, Bull Mastiff, Danish Broholmer, Dogue de Bordeaux, Great Swiss Mountain Dog, Korean Jindo, Kuvasz, Leonberger, Moscow Watchdog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Perro de Presa Mallorquin, Boerboel, Tibetan Mastiff.
countries.private_aviation: Must enter through an official port of entry. Give at least 48 hours' notice to the Inspection Unit of the confirmed arrival date, time, aircraft/flight and port of entry.
countries.authority: Turks and Caicos Islands Department of Agriculture – Animal Health Services Division
vaccinations: Rabies and other conditions are set out on the TCI import application and permit. The APHIS page doesn't state the timing, so confirm with the Department of Agriculture.
documents: TCI import permit.
International health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, signed in non-black ink, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement) BEFORE submitting the permit application. Valid 10 days from issue.
If the pet stays 24 hours or more in a transit country: a vet certificate covering that stay.

countries.name: Chad
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from Chad's ministry in charge of livestock (veterinary services) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Élevage et des Productions Animales — veterinary services (to be confirmed)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no Chad pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Togo
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip, current rabies vaccination, and a Togo-specific health certificate that USDA must ink-sign and emboss (no digital endorsement). No official rules were found for other origins or for an import permit.
countries.microchip: Required (US-origin certificate lists the microchip number as required and the vet must verify the chip).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3-4 weeks before travel: microchip and rabies vaccination, then an accredited-vet health certificate, then USDA ink endorsement (allow time for mail or appointment).
countries.authority: Togolese veterinary authority (not named by APHIS); USDA APHIS for US-origin certification
vaccinations: Rabies: current at the time of export; the certificate records vaccine name, batch number and validity end date (APHIS, US-origin)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to the Togolese Republic (AUG 2025 form), signed by an accredited vet (electronic signature accepted) and ink-endorsed and embossed by USDA; the original must travel with the pet

countries.name: Thailand
countries.summary: Apply to the Animal Quarantine Station (AQS) at the arrival airport for a DLD import permit, at least 7 and no more than 60 days before departure (30 days recommended). The pet needs a government-endorsed health certificate and is inspected at the AQS on arrival. There is no titre test and normally no quarantine when documents are complete.
countries.microchip: Microchip number required on the application and records. The DLD advises implanting it before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination.
countries.import_permit: Yes: DLD import permit, emailed by the AQS at the port of entry. Processing takes 5-7 Thai business days and the permit is valid 60 days. Owners travelling with their pet may apply on arrival if all originals are ready, but airlines may refuse boarding without a permit.
countries.quarantine: No fixed quarantine when documents are complete. The pet is inspected at the AQS on arrival. If documents are incomplete, the pet may be held at the quarantine station.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5-6 weeks: microchip, vaccines (21+ days before applying), permit request 30 days before departure, health certificate and endorsement within 10 days of arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: The Thai Embassy (Washington) says no dog breeds are banned, but airlines may restrict some. Minimum age 4 months (USDA summary).
countries.private_aviation: AQS offices are at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Samui and Krabi (all 24 hours for hand-carried pets; the Suvarnabhumi cargo AQS is open 08:30-16:30 Mon-Fri). The permit names the port of entry. No rule specific to private jets was found. Coordinate the arrival airport's AQS inspection and the FBO in advance.
countries.export: DLD: the microchip must be implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccine. Present the pet and documents at the departure port's quarantine station, ideally 2-3 days before departure, to get the export certificate.
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Development (DLD), Animal Quarantine Stations
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days before departure for a primary vaccine, given at 12 weeks of age or older. Boosters need no wait. Pets from rabies-free countries may be exempt.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, leptospirosis. If the leptospirosis vaccine is not valid or not 21+ days old, a negative leptospirosis test within 30 days before departure is accepted instead.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
documents: Application Form R.1/1 with pet details and microchip implantation certificate
Copy of owner's passport and flight itinerary
Colour photo of the pet
English vaccination certificates
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority (US: valid 10 days from USDA endorsement; originals only)
Printed import permit; Form R-6 and Import License R-7 issued at the AQS on arrival (500 THB per animal)

countries.name: Turkey
countries.summary: Max 2 pets per passenger. Each needs a microchip (before rabies vaccination), rabies vaccination, a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml (blood drawn 30+ days after vaccination, then a 90-day wait) and a health certificate issued within 2 days of travel. Several dog breeds are banned from entry.
countries.microchip: Required: ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or legible tattoo) applied before rabies vaccination; owner must supply reader if non-ISO
countries.rabies_titer: Required: ≥0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved lab, blood sampled ≥30 days after vaccination, and travel ≥3 months (90 days) after the test. Valid for life if boosters are never lapsed. Without a valid titer, 21-day quarantine and titer testing on arrival may apply (APHIS)
countries.parasite_treatment: APHIS guidance (US origin): tick (ectoparasite) treatment and Echinococcus (tapeworm) treatment within 30 days before travel, signed by vet
countries.quarantine: None if compliant; 21 days possible if titer missing or for young unvaccinated pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months: microchip → rabies vaccine → titer blood draw ≥30 days later → wait 3 months → tick + tapeworm treatment within 30 days → health certificate within 2 days of travel
countries.restricted_breeds: Import banned (Law 5199 Art. 14(1)(l) and Ministry dangerous-animals circular): American Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, and their crosses (list per Ministry; may change)
countries.private_aviation: Pets must enter through Ministry-approved border posts (approved port list on APHIS page). Effective 17 July 2026, Türkiye restricts dogs/cats from Texas and New Mexico (New World screwworm): no export from/transit via TX or NM
countries.export: Pet must be microchipped and registered in PETVET with a Turkish pet passport (foreign pets keep existing chip/passport). Rabies vaccine at ≥12 weeks, on/after chip date. FAVN titer (Etlik VKMAEM, ≥30 days after vaccination) if destination requires. Veterinary Health Certificate from the Provincial/District Directorate of Agriculture within 48 hours before departure. Protected native breeds (Kangal, Akbaş, Kars dog, Çatalburun, Zağar, Ankara cat, Van cat) need prior permission to leave; passports listing breed/colour only as 'mix' are rejected. Banned dangerous breeds may leave only if registered and destination accepts
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of the Republic of Türkiye (General Directorate of Food and Control; Veterinary Border Control Posts)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated or recombinant vaccine (not modified live), given on/after microchip date; booster after lapse counts as primary. Canada's CFIA notes Türkiye does not accept 3-year vaccine validity
Pets <3 months unvaccinated: admitted only under Ministry conditions (APHIS: 21-day home quarantine, or no-wildlife-contact declaration, or accompanied by vaccinated mother)
documents: Veterinary Health and Origin Certificate for cats/dogs/ferrets with passenger (one certificate per pet), issued by origin competent authority within 2 days before travel (US: APHIS endorsement ≤2 days before departure)
Pet passport or ID showing ownership
Original rabies titer report
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.summary: Apply for an import permit from the Chief Veterinary Officer at least 1 month ahead. Pets need an ISO microchip before rabies vaccination, a FAVN/RFFIT drawn at least 1 month after vaccination (lab emails results directly), a Brucella test for intact dogs, parasite treatment, a USDA-endorsed certificate within 7 days of arrival, and 2 working days' notice.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784 / 11785 Annex A, implanted before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN or RFFIT at an approved lab, at least 1 month after vaccination. The lab emails original results to aphmalmr@gmail.com. No post-test waiting period is stated, so confirm with the CVO.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment before export (timing not stated).
countries.import_permit: Required, held before entry. Apply to the Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, 80 Abercromby Street, Port of Spain (aphmalmr@gmail.com, 868-625-5997) at least 1 month before travel.
countries.quarantine: Not stated on the APHIS page. Confirm with the CVO whether home or facility quarantine applies.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN (1 month later, plus lab time), permit at least 1 month ahead, health certificate and endorsement within 7 days, 2 working days' notice.
countries.private_aviation: Notify the Veterinary Officer, Quarantine (868-693-2910, nadcaph2013@gmail.com) at least 2 working days before the scheduled arrival.
countries.export: Return to the US: Trinidad and Tobago is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, but it is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, Land and Fisheries
vaccinations: Rabies: required (timing beyond the FAVN rule isn't stated).
documents: Import permit ('Application for a permit to import dogs and cats').
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, endorsed by USDA within 7 days of arrival (digital VEHCS accepted), listing all countries of residence in the past 6 months.
Intact dogs: negative Brucella canis test.
